title: Maximum residue levels for milbemectin
summary: EU discusses increasing MRL for milbemectin on cherries
update: The European Union (EU) is discussing an increase in the maximum residue level (MRL) for milbemectin on sweet cherries.
what_changing: The EU is discussing an increase in the MRL for milbemectin on sweet cherries from the limit of determination (LOD) of 0.02 to 0.2 mg/kg. (The LOD is the lowest level that can be detected using the most modern and reliable analytical methods.)
why: Following an application for a change of this MRL by the producer of milbemectin, the European Food Safety Authority ( EFSA 2023 ) concluded that the proposed increase is unlikely to pose a risk to consumers’ health.
timeline: The new MRL is expected to apply from early 2027.
background: MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database . For further information on the setting of import tolerances, see Pesticide residue import tolerance MRLs explained .
resources: EFSA (2023) Peer review of the pesticide risk assessment of the active substance milbemectin . EFSA Journal, 21 (7): e08126.
